data.claim: _duplicate_work ignores needs entirely: A and B with B needs A are flagged. The scheduler orders by schedule.inherited_deps (own + ancestors' needs), and a dependency on a phase is unmet while any of its tasks is open, so a needs edge onto D orders the item after D and all of D's descendants.
data.falsifier: B needs A not flagged on current code, or E (in phase R needs Q) not blocked by Q's open task C
data.mechanism: progress._duplicate_work groups by tuple(sorted(globs)) only; schedule.dep_status returns unmet for a phase with open tasks; inherited_deps adds ancestor needs
data.probe: python3 scratchpad/probe.py: P{A x, B x needs A}, Q{C y}, P{D y}, R needs Q {E y}; detect(); inherited_deps(E); dep_status(Q)
data.probe_output: dup findings: [('A', '2 open items ... (x): A, B'), ('C', '3 open items ... (y): C, D, E')]; inherited E: [('R', 'Q')]; dep_status Q: (False, 'phase Q has 1 open task(s)')
data.question: Does _duplicate_work flag same-glob items that needs already orders, and which dependency graph orders items for the scheduler?

data.summary: schedule.critical_path(state, phase) slices the phase by direct parentage (phase in (i.parent, i.id)), so sub-tasks nested under a task are dropped and the reported wall-clock floor is too short. Probe: P > T > S1, S2 needs S1, S3 needs S2 -> critical_path(st,'P') == ['P'] while critical_path(st) == ['S1','S2','S3']. plan() already switched to state.tasks(phase) for this reason; critical_path is the stale copy (found by roborev duplication analysis, job 845, while on B-fix-dup-work-deps).

data.rule: Before warning that items 'cannot run in parallel', check whether inherited_deps (plus a dependency covering its descendants) already orders them; and when narrowing a group, apply the size threshold to the group, never to the narrowed subset.
